question: Is No Asteroids ("No Asteroid") free to play, and does Demo progress carry over?
answer: The full version of No Asteroids costs $7.99 on Steam (with a 20% launch discount to $6.39 until December 8, 2026). However, there is a free Steam Demo covering the first 15 days of the 90-day contract, and your save files automatically carry over to the full game if played on the same computer.

question: Is No Asteroids coming to PS5, Xbox, Switch, or Mobile?
answer: No console (PS5, Xbox, Nintendo Switch) or mobile (iOS/Android) versions have been announced as of launch. Currently, No Asteroids is exclusively available on PC (Windows 10+ 64-bit) and Apple Silicon macOS via Steam.

question: Does No Asteroids work on Steam Deck and Intel Macs?
answer: Intel-based Macs are explicitly NOT supported—macOS support requires an Apple Silicon (M1 or newer) chip. On Steam Deck, the game runs the Windows build through Steam's Proton compatibility layer; adjust graphics settings if voxel deformation causes frame drops.

question: Are there official cheat codes, console commands, or built-in mods?
answer: No. Unruled Games has not included official cheat codes, redeem codes, or built-in Steam Workshop mod support. If you want a relaxed playthrough without the 90-day pressure, choose the built-in No Rush mode.

question: How does 8-player online co-op work with shared money and saves?
answer: Campaign progress is saved on the host's PC across up to 5 save slots. Mined ore credits go into a shared crew wallet controlled by the host's permission settings, while hosts can toggle whether equipment loadouts are shared or personal. Use the T key for text chat and watch teammate outlines visible through rock.

question: Where is the No Asteroids save file located?
answer: On Windows, local save data typically sits under C:\Users\<YourUsername>\AppData\LocalLow\ (look for the Unruled Games / No Asteroids folder). On Steam Deck (Proton), check /home/deck/.local/share/Steam/steamapps/compatdata/5527800/pfx/drive_c/users/steamuser/AppData/LocalLow/.

question: How is No Asteroids different from Drink the Ocean?
answer: Both are viral first-person incremental simulation games with absurd premises, which is why they often appear together in search trends. No Asteroids (by Unruled Games, $7.99 on Steam) has you mine a 5,000,000 m³ asteroid in 90 days solo or in 8-player co-op. Drink the Ocean (by Pinidi Studio) is a free browser/mobile incremental game where you drink the world's oceans through a straw.
